concepts.title: Classifying Organohalides by Halogen Count and Carbon Framework
concepts.definition: Organohalides sort first by how many halogen atoms they carry, then monohalides sort again by the kind of carbon holding the halogen: an sp3 carbon in an alkyl group, an sp3 carbon beside a double bond or aromatic ring, or an sp2 carbon of a double bond or ring.
concepts.key_idea: Allylic and benzylic labels describe sp3 carbons that neighbour a C=C or a ring; vinylic and aryl labels describe sp2 carbons, which resist substitution.
concepts.textbook_ref: lech201.txt section 6.1, classification tree and examples (lines ~103-160)

solution_steps.action: locate the carbon bonded to the halogen
solution_steps.explain: every class label hangs on this one carbon

solution_steps.action: read its hybridisation and its neighbours
solution_steps.explain: sp3 next to C=C means allylic, sp3 next to a ring means benzylic, sp3 in a plain chain means alkyl (1, 2 or 3 degree by attached carbons), sp2 on C=C means vinylic, sp2 in a ring means aryl

concepts.title: IUPAC Naming of Haloalkanes and Haloarenes
concepts.definition: IUPAC names treat the halogen as a prefix on the parent hydrocarbon: take the longest chain containing the halogen-bearing carbon, number it so substituents get the lowest locants, and order prefixes alphabetically.
concepts.key_idea: gem-dihalides keep both halogens on one carbon while vic-dihalides place them on neighbouring carbons; o-, m-, p- of the common system become 1,2-, 1,3-, 1,4- in IUPAC.
concepts.textbook_ref: lech201.txt section 6.2 with Table 6.1 name pairs (lines ~161-233)

solution_steps.action: pick the parent chain through the C-X carbon

solution_steps.action: number for lowest locants and list prefixes
solution_steps.explain: halo and alkyl prefixes go alphabetically with their positions

concepts.title: Making Haloalkanes from Alcohols
concepts.definition: The -OH group of an alcohol gives way to a halogen on treatment with a concentrated halogen acid, a phosphorus halide, or thionyl chloride; SOCl2 is the cleanest choice because SO2 and HCl leave as gases and the halide needs no distilling.
concepts.key_idea: Primary and secondary alcohols need ZnCl2 with dry HCl, tertiary alcohols react on mere shaking with concentrated HCl, and the alcohol reactivity order with one haloacid runs 3 > 2 > 1.

solution_steps.action: match the alcohol class to the reagent
solution_steps.explain: 3 degree alcohols react with concentrated HCl alone; 1 and 2 degree need ZnCl2 catalyst

solution_steps.action: check the by-product route for purity
solution_steps.explain: SOCl2 wins because gaseous SO2 and HCl escape, leaving the halide behind

concepts.title: Halogen Exchange: Finkelstein and Swarts Reactions
concepts.definition: Halogen swap reactions cover the halides other syntheses miss: NaI in dry acetone turns an alkyl chloride or bromide into the iodide (Finkelstein), and a metal fluoride such as AgF, Hg2F2, CoF2 or SbF3 delivers the fluoride (Swarts).
concepts.key_idea: NaCl or NaBr precipitates out of dry acetone, pulling the Finkelstein equilibrium toward the iodide exactly as Le Chatelier predicts.

solution_steps.action: identify which halide is wanted
solution_steps.explain: iodides come from NaI in acetone; fluorides come from Swarts metal fluorides

solution_steps.action: write the departing halogen salt
solution_steps.explain: the NaCl or NaBr by-product precipitating in acetone drives the exchange forward

concepts.title: Aryl Halides via Diazonium Salts (Sandmeyer Route)
concepts.definition: Diazotising a primary aromatic amine in cold mineral acid builds a diazonium salt; cuprous chloride or cuprous bromide then replaces the diazonium group with Cl or Br, while potassium iodide alone installs iodine.
concepts.key_idea: Direct iodination of arenes is reversible and needs an oxidant for the HI formed, so the diazonium route is the practical entry to aryl iodides.
concepts.textbook_ref: lech201.txt section 6.5, Sandmeyer and electrophilic substitution (lines ~450-468)

solution_steps.action: swap the diazonium group for the halogen
solution_steps.explain: CuCl or CuBr gives the aryl chloride or bromide; KI alone gives the aryl iodide

concepts.title: Boiling Point, Melting Point and Density Trends of Halides
concepts.definition: Polarity plus extra electrons make halide boiling points sit above those of parent hydrocarbons; with one fixed alkyl group the boiling order runs RI > RBr > RCl > RF, branching pushes boiling points down, and symmetry lifts the melting point of para-dihalobenzenes above their ortho and meta isomers.
concepts.key_idea: Bromo, iodo and polychloro derivatives are denser than water, and haloalkanes stay nearly insoluble in water because no comparably strong attractions replace broken hydrogen bonds.
concepts.textbook_ref: lech201.txt section 6.6, Fig 6.1, Table 6.3 and solubility (lines ~487-580)

solution_steps.explain: branching cuts contact area so boiling point drops; para symmetry packs the crystal so melting point rises

solution_steps.action: follow halogen mass down the group
solution_steps.explain: heavier, more polarisable halogens strengthen dispersion forces and add density

concepts.title: SN2 Kinetics: Bimolecular Substitution Rate
concepts.definition: A bimolecular substitution is a single backside attack in which bond making and bond breaking happen together, so the rate tracks both concentrations: rate constant times halide molarity times nucleophile molarity.
concepts.key_idea: Crowding around the reacting carbon sets the speed order primary > secondary > tertiary, and every SN2 event inverts the configuration like an umbrella in wind.
concepts.textbook_ref: lech201.txt section 6.7.1(a), SN2 mechanism and Fig 6.2-6.3 (lines ~726-813)

solution_steps.action: multiply the two molarities
solution_steps.explain: the bimolecular rate law needs the product of the halide and nucleophile concentrations

solution_steps.action: scale by the rate constant
solution_steps.explain: the second-order rate constant converts the concentration product into a rate

concepts.title: SN1 Kinetics: Unimolecular Substitution Rate
concepts.definition: An unimolecular substitution runs through a slow ionisation that frees a planar carbocation, so only the alkyl halide molarity governs the rate; halide molarity is moles divided by litres, then scaled by the rate constant.
concepts.key_idea: Carbocation stability puts tertiary, benzylic and allylic halides on top for SN1, and attack on either face of the flat intermediate racemises a chiral substrate.
concepts.textbook_ref: lech201.txt section 6.7.1(b), SN1 mechanism with tert-butyl bromide (lines ~814-932)
question_patterns: 0.06 mol of tert-butyl bromide is made up to 300 mL; with k = 0.0045 per second find the initial SN1 rate

solution_steps.action: convert moles and volume to molarity
solution_steps.explain: the rate law uses concentration, so divide the dissolved moles by the volume in litres

solution_steps.action: scale by the first-order constant
solution_steps.explain: only the alkyl halide enters the rate because ionisation is the slow step

concepts.title: Optical Activity and Specific Rotation
concepts.definition: A polarimeter reads the angle by which a chiral sample twists plane-polarised light; dividing that reading by tube length in decimetres and by solution concentration gives the specific rotation, a fingerprint of the compound itself.
concepts.key_idea: A plus sign marks clockwise (dextrorotatory) twist and a minus sign anticlockwise (laevorotatory) twist, but neither sign reveals the absolute configuration.
concepts.textbook_ref: lech201.txt section 6.7.1(c)(i), polarimeter and d/l forms (lines ~891-905)
question_patterns: a 1.0 dm tube holds a solution of 0.20 g per mL and the polarimeter reads +2.6 degrees; find the specific rotation

solution_steps.action: normalise the reading per decimetre
solution_steps.explain: longer tubes proportionally rotate light further, so divide the observed angle by tube length

solution_steps.explain: rotation also scales with how much solute each millilitre carries

concepts.title: Racemic Mixtures and Enantiomeric Excess
concepts.definition: Mirror-image isomers rotate light equally but oppositely, so an equal-amount mixture reads zero; comparing a sample rotation with the pure enantiomer rotation measures how far the mixture sits from racemic, expressed as a percentage.
concepts.key_idea: SN1 solvolysis of an optically active halide racemises it because the flat carbocation is attacked from both faces, unlike SN2 which inverts cleanly.
concepts.textbook_ref: lech201.txt section 6.7.1(c), racemisation and SN1 vs SN2 stereochemistry (lines ~1016-1104)
question_patterns: the pure enantiomer of a compound rotates at +9.0 degrees and a sample reads +4.5 degrees; find the enantiomeric excess

solution_steps.action: form the rotation ratio
solution_steps.explain: sample rotation divided by pure-enantiomer rotation equals the fraction of net excess

solution_steps.action: convert the fraction to a percentage
solution_steps.explain: multiplying by 100 reports the enantiomeric excess on the percent scale

concepts.title: Ambident Nucleophiles: KCN versus AgCN
concepts.definition: Cyanide and nitrite ions offer two attacking atoms, so the counter-ion picks the product: ionic KCN frees cyanide ions that attack through carbon to give nitriles, whereas covalent AgCN leaves nitrogen to attack, giving isocyanides.
concepts.key_idea: The same ambident logic separates KNO2, which yields alkyl nitrites through oxygen, from AgNO2, which yields nitroalkanes through nitrogen.
concepts.textbook_ref: lech201.txt section 6.7.1, ambident nucleophiles and Table 6.4, Example 6.5 (lines ~646-748)

solution_steps.action: read the counter-ion character
solution_steps.explain: ionic K+ salts release the free ion; covalent Ag+ salts tie up one end so the other atom attacks

solution_steps.action: name the linking atom and the product class
solution_steps.explain: carbon attack gives cyanides or nitro compounds; nitrogen attack gives isocyanides or nitrites

concepts.title: Dehydrohalogenation and the Saytzeff Rule
concepts.definition: Alcoholic KOH strips HX from a haloalkane: the halogen leaves the alpha carbon and a hydrogen leaves a neighbouring beta carbon, building an alkene; when several beta positions exist, the alkene with more alkyl groups on its double-bond carbons dominates.
concepts.key_idea: Only beta hydrogens can leave, so counting distinct beta positions tells you how many alkenes are possible before applying Saytzeff to rank them.
concepts.textbook_ref: lech201.txt section 6.7.1(2), elimination and Saytzeff rule (lines ~1105-1134)
question_patterns: predict the major alkene when 2-bromopentane is heated with alcoholic KOH

solution_steps.action: mark alpha and beta carbons
solution_steps.explain: the halogen carbon is alpha; each adjacent carbon is a possible beta site for hydrogen loss

solution_steps.action: rank the possible alkenes by substitution
solution_steps.explain: the double bond carrying more alkyl groups is the Saytzeff product and dominates

concepts.title: Haloarene Reactivity and Ortho-Para Direction
concepts.definition: Ring-bound halogens shrug off nucleophilic attack: resonance lends the C-X bond partial double-bond character, the sp2 ring carbon grips the electron pair more tightly than an sp3 carbon would, and a phenyl cation cannot survive; yet that same resonance directs electrophilic substitution to ortho and para even while the -I effect deactivates the ring.
concepts.key_idea: An electron-withdrawing -NO2 group accelerates nucleophilic displacement from ortho or para (where resonance parks the carbanion charge on it) but never from meta.
concepts.textbook_ref: lech201.txt section 6.7.2, low NS reactivity, NO2 effect, EAS orientation (lines ~1186-1281)
question_patterns: explain why chlorobenzene resists nucleophilic substitution compared with a chloroalkane

solution_steps.action: test for resonance and hybridisation effects
solution_steps.explain: partial double-bond character plus a shorter, tighter sp2 C-X bond blocks the SN routes and an unstable phenyl cation rules out SN1

solution_steps.action: check the directing pattern
solution_steps.explain: resonance donation raises electron density at ortho and para, so electrophiles attack there while the stronger -I effect slows the ring overall
